msg.content:
1	# Application Framework Changelog
     2	
     3	## v7.1.0 - OpenAPI Generator & API Cache (Breaking-S)
     4	- API: Added automatic OpenAPI 3.1 spec generation from registered API methods.
     5	- API: New `GetOpenAPISpec` method serves the generated spec as raw JSON.
     6	- API: Added `HtaccessGenerator` for API URL rewriting via `.htaccess`.
     7	- API: Added response schema inference from PHP return arrays.
     8	- API: OpenAPI spec link added to the API methods meta navigation.
     9	- API: Added response schemas to `GetAppCountriesAPI` and `GetAppLocalesAPI`.
    10	- API Cache: Renamed `FixedDurationStrategy` duration constants to underscore format.
    11	- API Cache: Added matching short-duration constants to `FixedDurationStrategy`.
    12	- API Cache: `readFromCache()` now logs corrupt cache files before auto-removing.
    13	- API Cache: Hardened `readFromCache()` error logging against logger failures.
    14	- API Cache: Improved `readFromCache()` PHPDoc for corrupt-cache return case.
    15	- API Cache: Added `@throws` annotation to `invalidateMethod()`.
    16	- AI Cache: Added explicit `filemtime()` false-guard in `FixedDurationStrategy`.
    17	- Deepl: Fixed incorrect `makeError()` call, replaced with `makeDangerous()`.
    18	- Deepl: Removed deprecated language code workaround, now handled upstream.
    19	- Deepl: Fixed double-instantiation in test screen.
    20	- Docs: Added PHPStan baseline regeneration rule to constraints.
    21	- Docs: Documented YAML colon+space constraint for module keyword values.
    22	- Docs: Added "Trait Consumer Policy" to coding constraints.
    23	- Composer: Build now generates `openapi.json` and API `.htaccess`.
    24	- Composer: Fixed build artefacts output path for framework-internal builds.
    25	- Tests: Added 11 test files covering the OpenAPI module.
    26	- Tests: Migrated 19 legacy test files to namespaced `*Test.php` convention.
    27	- Tests: Fixed `HtaccessGeneratorTest` assertions for empty default rewrite base.
    28	- Tests: Fixed `RecordTieInTest` inter-test pollution via `tearDown()` cleanup.
    29	- Tests: Added `live-http` PHPUnit group excluding live-server tests by default.
    30	- Tests: Added `CountryRequestScreen` as `CountryRequestTrait` consumer.
    31	- Dependencies: Bumped up AppUtils Collections to [v1.2.2](https://github.com/Mistralys/application-utils-collections/releases/tag/1.2.2).
    32	
    33	### Breaking Changes
    34	
    35	`FixedDurationStrategy` duration constants were renamed from compressed format
    36	(`DURATION_1MIN`) to underscore-separated (`DURATION_1_MIN`). Find-and-replace
    37	all consumer references.
    38	
    39	## v7.0.13 - Markdown Renderer Docs
    40	- MarkdownRenderer: Added full module documentation and CTX integration.
    41	
    42	## v7.0.12 - DeepL Target Language Fix
    43	- DeeplHelper: Fixed deprecated language codes causing exceptions; now resolved to regional locales.
    44	- Tests: Added `DeeplHelperTest` integration test to verify correct target language code resolution.
    45	- Deepl: Fixed an exception in the test screen.
    46	- Dependencies: Updated DeepL XML Translator to [v3.0.1](https://github.com/Mistralys/deepl-xml-translator/releases/tag/3.0.1).
    47	
    48	## v7.0.12-dev - User-Scoped API Response Caching
    49	- API: Added user-scoped caching via `UserScopedCacheInterface` and trait.
    50	- API: User scope key injected automatically, preventing silent omission.
    51	- API: Empty user identifier now throws instead of silent fallback.
    52	
    53	## v7.0.11-dev - API Response Caching
    54	- API: Added file-based response caching for API methods.
    55	- API: Strategies: `FixedDurationStrategy` (TTL) and `ManualOnlyStrategy`.
    56	- API: Caching opt-in via interface + trait, matching existing patterns.
    57	- API: Cache location registered in admin CacheControl UI via event handler.
    58	
    59	## v7.0.11 - Deepl Settings Overrides
    60	- Deepl: Added DB-based app setting overrides for the API key and proxy configuration.

msg.content: 1 2 3 # Application Framework 4 5 All-in-one PHP framework and UI layer for building web and intranet 6 applications. 7 8 ## Introduction 9 10 The framework is designed to be a solid foundation for custom-built web 11 applications. The integrated functionality helps to focus on the application 12 logic, while being able to create the necessary administration screens, 13 APIs and more with minimal effort. 14 15 Note that it is not a CMS: it is exclusively a tool for building custom 16 applications. Supporting features are available out of the box, like the 17 notepad or image library, but anything your application needs to do must 18 be implemented by you. 19 20 One of the core functionalities of the framework is to provide an extensive 21 ecology of classes for accessing custom data stored in the database. 22 This includes complex filtering capabilities as well as a versioning 23 system with record state tracking (draft, published, etc.). 24 25 ## Features overview 26 27 - PHP helper classes for UI elements 28 - Form building system - every screen is a form 29 - Rule-based application environment detection 30 - Advanced database-stored data handling tools 31 - Class-based extensible templating system 32 - Localization system for UI translation 33 - News central (release notes, etc.) 34 - Event handling system 35 - Image media library and UI 36 - Tagging system and UI 37 - Versioning system with state tracking 38 - Disposables system for automated garbage collection 39 - API response caching (file-based, opt-in via Interface + Trait; TTL and manual strategies) 40 - SSO via CAS 41 - Interface Translations: English, German, French 42 - Build-time module documentation generators (Modules Overview, Keyword Glossary) 43 - Own ecology of supporting libraries 44 45 ## Requirements 46 47 - PHP 7.4 or higher (fully PHP 8 compatible) 48 - [Composer](https://getcomposer.org) 49 - MariaDB or MySQL database with InnoDB support 50 - Webserver 51 52 ## Installation 53 54 The framework can be installed as a regular Composer dependency. 55 However, the required application skeleton of folders and files 56 can currently only be generated dynamically using the 57 [Framework Manager][], which is currently still a private project. 58 59 Documentation on how to set up an application using the framework 60 is still in progress. In the meantime, the example application can 61 be used as a reference (see [Example application](#example-application)). 62 63 ## Example application 64 65 The framework includes a sample application which is used as a reference for 66 available features, best practices, and testing. It can also be used as 67 the basis for a new application. 68 69 You will find it in the `tests/application` folder. 70 71 **Installation** 72 73 1. Import the SQL file `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` into a database. 74 2. Open the folder `tests/application/config`. 75 3. Copy `test-db-config.dist.php` to `test-db-config.php`. 76 4. Copy `test-ui-config.dist.php` to `test-ui-config.php`. 77 5. Edit the settings in both files. 78 6. Access the `tests/application` folder via the webserver. 79 80 ## Composer commands 81 82 These are custom Composer commands that are available 83 when developing locally. 84 85 ### Build 86 87 The build step generates module documentation artefacts from `module-context.yaml` 88 files discovered throughout the codebase, updates the CTX `generated-at.txt` 89 timestamp, regenerates the API method index, and rebuilds offline event listeners. 90 91 ```bash 92 composer build 93 ``` 94 95 For the full development build (includes module glossary and keyword index): 96 97 ```bash 98 composer build-dev 99 ```

1	## Coding Patterns
     2	
     3	## Checking instance types
     4	
     5	Use the `ClassHelper` static methods to check for class types. This will throw
     6	an exception if the type does not match, and guarantees that static analyzers
     7	like PHPStan can infer the correct type after the check.
     8	
     9	```php
    10	<?php
    11	use AppUtils\ClassHelper;
    12	
    13	$campaign = ClassHelper::requireObjectInstanceOf(
    14	    CampaignRecord::class,
    15	    $record
    16	);
    17	```
    18	
    19	## Creating Objects Lazily
    20	
    21	Use `isset()` for the property to initialize it as needed.
    22	
    23	```php
    24	<?php
    25	
    26	class CampaignService 
    27	{
    28	    private ?CampaignManager $campaignManager = null;
    29	
    30	    public function getCampaignManager() : CampaignManager 
    31	    {
    32	        if (!isset($this->campaignManager)) {
    33	            $this->object = new CampaignManager();
    34	        }
    35	        
    36	        return $this->campaignManager;
    37	    }
    38	}
    39	```

1	# Coding Guidelines
     2	
     3	## General Conventions
     4	
     5	- **Null checks**: prefer `isset($this->property)` over strict `null` comparisons.
     6	- **Exception Workflow**: 
     7	- **Keep It Left**: minimize nesting by returning early from functions.
     8	- **Avoid long functions**: break down complex logic into smaller private methods.
     9	- **Consistent naming**: snake_case for DB fields; camelCase for PHP properties/methods.
    10	- **Short acronyms like "ID"**: Always keep uppercase, e.g., `getID()`,  `getUserID()`.
    11	- **Array Initialization**: Always define arrays with the verbose `array()` syntax.
